discovery.title: Revisit saved leads first
discovery.steps: Search the inventory, held notes, provider catalog and source guides. Deduplicate by organization and canonical page, and keep prior failures and uncertainties.

discovery.title: Probe public structured feeds
discovery.steps: Look for permitted iCalendar, RSS, official API, JSON-LD, sitemaps or stable HTML. Check robots and access terms, cache raw evidence, record zero-match or errors, and build a focused adapter before using model tokens.

discovery.title: Find Amsterdam providers and directories
discovery.steps: Search neighborhood venues, libraries, municipal agendas, activity providers and directories using Dutch and English terms for drop-in, one-off, social dance, walks, workshops and community events, with Waterlooplein and Oosterdok as location clues.

discovery.title: Follow aggregators to organizers
discovery.steps: Use Meetup, Hipsy, Eventbrite, ClassPass and city directories to find organizers. Prefer an accessible public organizer calendar or feed; record both links and avoid duplicating the same event.

discovery.title: Use Luna for unresolved extraction
discovery.steps: Once code cannot reliably extract the needed facts, give Luna one source guide, the smallest relevant cached excerpts or links, date range and output schema. Save successful and failed evidence, not just conclusions.

discovery.title: Escalate only the unresolved problem
discovery.steps: Use a stronger review for conflicting dates, costs or eligibility. A browser or previously authorized Android route can help with ordinary rendering gaps. Respect access gates and rate limits; model choice does not grant access.
